In Chinese criminal law, crimes include "伪造、变造国家机关证件、印章罪" (forgery of state documents) and "买卖国家机关证件、印章罪". Also "非法买卖国家机关证件罪". The act of selling a forged document is "非法买卖国家机关证件、印章罪". Also possibly "伪造国家机关证件罪". The person sold a forged document, which is a false certificate. The crime could be "伪造国家机关证件罪" (forgery) and "非法买卖国家机关证件罪". However Chinese law distinguishes: If one forges a certificate, that's "伪造国家机关证件、印章罪". If one sells forged certificates, that's "非法买卖国家机关证件、印章罪". The fact says he sold a forged "流动人口婚育证明". The act of forging is implied? He sold a forged document; the forging itself is a crime, but the fact only mentions selling. It says "以人民币30元的价格贩卖了一本伪造的...". So the crime is "非法买卖国家机关证件、印章罪". Also possibly "伪造国家机关证件罪" if he also forged. But the fact doesn't state he forged, only that the document was forged. Could be that he possessed a forged document and sold it, which is illegal sale. So the appropriate charge: "非法买卖国家机关证件、印章罪". Also maybe "伪造国家机关证件罪" if he created it. The safe answer: single crime.
